text:
Reprints 
Here's your Investing Action Plan for Thursday: what you need to know as an investor for the coming day. 
X The day in earnings will start with Chinese tech giant Alibaba ( BABA ) and end with U.S. tech leaders Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ). Also on what will be a frantic day for quarterly reports, Visa ( V ), Mastercard ( MA ), and UPS ( UPS ) will also come out. Meanwhile, General Motors ( GM ), Ford ( F ) and other carmakers will report monthly U.S. sales figures. Apple 
The iPhone maker reports fiscal Q1 results after the close. 
Estimates : EPS to rise 13.7% to $3.82 as revenue grows 10% to $86.29 billion, according to Zacks Investment Research. 
Stock : Shares were flat at 166.93 on the stock market today. Apple has tumbled about 7% since hitting an all-time high of 180.10 on Jan. 18. 
Apple is facing a flurry of reports that iPhone X demand is waning, leading to production cuts at contract manufacturers in Asia. The Q1 report will be the first to include sales from the iPhone X as well as iPhone 8 series handsets. 
On Wednesday, BMO Capital Markets downgraded Apple and slashed its price target on concerns that the iPhone maker is "hitting a plateau." Amazon 
The e-commerce giant will report Q4 results after the market close. 
Estimates : EPS to climb 20% to $1.85 as revenue grows 37% to $60.03 billion. 
Stock : Shares were up 1.5% at 1,459.49. 
Analysts will be listening for comments surrounding Amazon's line of consumer electronics after a better-than-expected holiday sales performance. 
"We think Q4 will be another impressive holiday quarter for Amazon, and believe the recent focus on hardware launches may intensify purchase activity on Amazon.com," wrote Canaccord Genuity analyst Michael Graham recently. Alphabet 
The Google parent reports Q4 financials after the close. 
Estimates : EPS is expected to grow 34% to $10.12, with revenue rising 21% to $25.66 billion. 
Stock : Shares were down 0.2% at 1,175.75. 
Google's traffic acquisition costs, what it pays partner websites to carry ads, have been rising and remain a concern. Some analysts are looking for management commentary on stock repurchases in light of lowered taxes on overseas cash brought back to the U.S. Google's growing rivalry with Amazon in voice search and smart home devices could be another earnings call topic. Alibaba 
China's e-commerce leader will report before the market opens. 
Estimates : EPS to rise 27% to $1.65 as revenue surges 58% to $12.13 billion, marking its strongest top-line growth in 15 quarters. 
Stock : Shares were up 2.2% at 204.09. 
Analysts will want to hear more about user growth and investments in new retail initiatives that will accelerate this year. Alibaba is continuing a major push into brick-and-mortar retailing with plans to add 30 supermarkets in Beijing. IBD'S TAKE: By learning to use call options , investors can significantly reduce risk and capitalize on basing stocks that are making breakaway gains caused by earnings reports. Other Earnings 
Visa ( V ) is expected to grow fiscal Q1 EPS by 14% to 98 cents on revenue of $4.81 billion, up 8%. 
Mastercard ( MA ) is seen reporting a 30% jump in Q4 EPS to $1.12, as revenue climbs 18% to $3.26 billion. 
UPS ( UPS ) is expected to report 1% EPS growth to $1.65 on a 7% rise in revenue to $18.19 billion. 
Edwards Lifesciences ( EW ) is expected to report EPS of 90 cents on $863 million in sales, up a respective 20% and 12.4%. 
Boston Scientific's ( BSX ) EPS is seen rising 13% to 34 cents, as sales grow 8% to $2.37 billion. U.S. Auto Sales 
Sales are expected to cool in January, with car info site Edmunds seeing a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 16.7 million, down sharply from December's pace of 17.9 million, which was helped by holiday incentives. Ford should see sales of new cars, trucks and SUVs fall 7% from a year ago, and Fiat Chrysler ( FCAU ) could see a 15% decline. But GM should see sales rise 4% while Toyota Motors ( TM ) grows sales 8%.
